synthesis:draft.headline: VIC1 five-minute minimum RRP was -504.6525 $/MWh at 2026-07-28 21:20 AEST
summary: Minimum five-minute RRP in VIC1: -504.6525 $/MWh at 2026-07-28 21:20 AEST (interval end) (evidence: ev0483).
The negative-price episode around that interval covered two five-minute intervals (evidence: ev0002).
Operational demand in the half-hour containing the price extreme (half-hour ending 11:30 UTC = 2026-07-28 21:30 AEST) was 7491.0 MW (evidence: ev0951).
Maximum operational demand in the window was 8131.0 MW (evidence: ev0973).
AEMO invoked automated constraint set CA_SYDS_597A8B26 from 11:00 hrs (market notice, citation c1).
Forecast-versus-actual demand metrics for the 05:30–17:30 UTC window: mean error (POE50 − actual) = -183.96 MW (evidence: ev1103) and MAE = 186.88 MW (evidence: ev1102).

numeric_claims.text: Number of five-minute intervals in the negative-price episode around the minimum
Operational demand in the half-hour containing the price extreme (half-hour ending 11:30 UTC)
Maximum operational demand in the window
Forecast mean error (POE50 − actual) for the window

possible_explanations.statement: Constraint automation invoked from 11:00 (see notice c1) might have changed interconnector binding conditions or effective transfer capability and could be associated with counter‑price conditions in the 11:15–11:25 UTC window.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Obtain 5‑minute binding‑constraint logs and shadow prices plus interconnector flow records for 11:00–11:30 UTC to see whether CA_SYDS_597A8B26 or related constraints were binding and what shadow prices/flows they produced.

possible_explanations.statement: An excess of dispatchable or low‑marginal‑cost generation relative to demand (or rapid changes in unit outputs around that time) might have coincided with the negative RRP.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Retrieve 5‑minute generation-by-unit and by-fuel dispatch, and unit offer/offer stack for 11:10–11:25 UTC to compare supply availability and offers against demand and interconnector export capacity.

possible_explanations.statement: Unit non‑conformance or specific unit dispatch/rebid events (for example the TRGBESS1 non‑conformance reported on 2026-07-27 in notice c3) might have been relevant to system balancing in the window.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Obtain unit availability/offers and the rebid history for TRGBESS1 and other units with large SCADA changes, and cross-check timing with the negative-price five‑minute intervals.

possible_explanations.statement: Forecast/dispatch timing differences (POE50 forecasts were frequently lower than actual in the morning window) might have interacted with dispatch decisions and constraint management around the event.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare pre-dispatch runs available immediately before dispatch with actual dispatch outcomes and review any constraint or FCAS enablement decisions made in the pre-dispatch/dispatch cycle for 11:00–11:30 UTC.

uncertainties: No binding-constraint logs or shadow-price values (5‑minute) are available in the provided evidence, so it is unclear which constraints, if any, were binding at 11:20 UTC.
Five‑minute interconnector flow (NETINTERCHANGE) at 11:20 UTC was not returned by the called tools; the precise export/import balance at the minimum-price interval is therefore uncertain.

Unit offer stacks and rebid histories for the exact five‑minute intervals are not available in the evidence returned, limiting ability to identify whether negative offers or rebids were active at 11:15–11:25 UTC.

Five-minute interconnector NETINTERCHANGE flows for VIC1 at the intervals 11:15 and 11:20 UTC on 2026-07-28.
Unit-level offers and rebid history (including negative offers) for major generators and TRGBESS1 around 11:00–11:30 UTC.
Five-minute generation-by-fuel or full unit dispatch records for 11:00–11:30 UTC to quantify supply changes at the time.
